summary: At 08:20:00Z deploy dep-0414 (commit ef5484e, 'idempotency: shorter keys') went live in fivo-api. It changed build_key from user_id:device_id:client_seq to user_id:client_seq. client_seq is a per-device counter, so a user's second device can now produce a key that already exists. That insert violates the global constraint uq_transactions_idempotency_key, and neither write route catches IntegrityError, so POST /transactions and POST /transactions/quick-add return 500. Roll back to 7bc71c8 now. The one inferred link is that the colliding rows come from another device; no failing request's key has been paired with an existing row.

root_cause.component: app/services/idempotency.py build_key (dep-0414, ef5484e), with unique constraint uq_transactions_idempotency_key and unhandled IntegrityError on the write routes
root_cause.summary: The deploy dropped device_id from the idempotency key, while the replay check find_replay is still device-scoped and the DB constraint is global. Cross-device seq overlap for the same user now collides and surfaces as an unhandled UniqueViolation, returned as a 500.

hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-0414 (ef5484e) dropped device_id from the idempotency key, so keys collide across a user's devices and writes fail with an unhandled UniqueViolation (500).

supporting.statement: Deploy went live at 08:20:00Z and is the only deploy; no config changes were recorded.
The diff touches one file and one line: build_key lost device_id.
The global unique constraint exists, find_replay is device-scoped, and neither route handles IntegrityError.
Sampled error lines are UniqueViolation on uq_transactions_idempotency_key, first at 08:22:31; 75 of 77 errors in 08:20-09:00 are of this type.
All 111 rows saved from 08:20:20 use the short key and none use the old format; pre-deploy rows use user:device:seq.
10 post-08:20 rows across 9 users share user_id and client_seq with an earlier row from a different device, showing cross-device seq overlap is common.

contradicting.statement: No failing request's key was paired with an existing row from another device; logs carry neither client_seq nor the key.
Only 77 error lines were classified (08:20-09:00) against 89 error lines in the wider window; the type of the remainder is unchecked.
2 ConnectionResetError lines (one is GET /categories at 08:20:58) are unexplained but are not on the main failure path.

hypotheses.statement: A neon-postgres problem (suspended compute, pool exhaustion, slow or locked writes) is causing write timeouts, as in INC-2026-024.

supporting.statement: A past incident had a 5xx spike on POST /transactions from a suspended DB compute.

contradicting.statement: 0 log lines matching QueuePool, OperationalError or connection refused from 08:20 to 09:00.
The 500s are fast (12-17 ms) UniqueViolations, so the database is up and rejecting duplicate keys.

hypotheses.statement: The Redis queue or fivo-worker path is failing, causing 500s on quick-add and transaction writes.

supporting.statement: quick-add waits on the worker through the Redis queue.

contradicting.statement: 0 lines matching 'redis' or 'timeout' in fivo-api from 08:20 to 09:00.
fivo-worker logged no errors and had no deploys.
The observed errors are Postgres unique violations.

hypotheses.statement: A client-side change (new app release, bad or missing client_seq) hits a latent write-path bug, independent of the deploy.

supporting.statement: After 08:20 a user's saved rows show one device's seq run advancing with the other device's seqs missing. This fits rejected writes, and H1 explains it equally well.

contradicting.statement: Failures are spread across many iOS and Android devices, and several devices both succeed and fail in the same window.
client_seq runs consecutively per device across 08:20, with no resets or duplicates.
The key format switched exactly at the deploy time.
A single server-side constraint conflict dominates the errors.

facts.statement: dep-0414 (ef5484ec, previous 7bc71c84) went live in fivo-api at 2026-11-10T08:20:00Z; it is the only deploy found, and no config changes were recorded 04:00-09:02.
The deploy changes only app/services/idempotency.py, one line: the key lost device_id.
Neither POST /transactions nor quick-add catches IntegrityError, and the unique constraint on idempotency_key is global.
In 08:12-09:02, /transactions returned 79 500s (1 in baseline) and quick-add returned 9 500s with 17 201s (0 500s in baseline).
Error logs begin in the 08:20 bucket and stay elevated through 09:00.
Of 77 error lines in 08:20-09:00, 67 were on /transactions, 9 on quick-add and 1 on /categories; 75 are UniqueViolation on uq_transactions_idempotency_key and 2 are ConnectionResetError.
The first sampled UniqueViolation is at 08:22:31. The failures are fast and repeat from the same device, which looks like client retries.
All 111 rows saved 08:20:20-09:01:52 (46 users) use the user:seq key; none use the old format.
There are 0 matches for QueuePool, OperationalError, timeout, connection refused or redis in fivo-api errors, and fivo-worker logged no errors.

assumptions: The colliding existing rows come from a different device of the same user. This is inferred from the code and data; no failing request's key was paired with an existing row.
The roughly 12 error lines outside the classified 08:20-09:00 window (between 09:00 and 09:02) are assumed to be the same failure.
The 2 ConnectionResetError lines and the 1 baseline /transactions 500 are assumed to be unrelated noise.
Neon, Redis and the external dependencies were not checked directly; they are assumed healthy because no log lines point to them.
Exact onset is bounded by the 5-minute log buckets.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back fivo-api to 7bc71c84 (revert ef5484e / dep-0414).
recommended_actions.rationale: Restores the device-scoped key user:device:seq, which stops the new collisions. The 5xx started with the deploy at 08:20 and was still occurring at 09:00.

recommended_actions.action: Ask support to tell the two affected mobile users to retry once the rollback is live.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rejected inserts are rolled back, so those entries were not saved.

recommended_actions.action: Before re-shipping shorter keys, keep device_id in the key or make the replay check and constraint consistent. Catch IntegrityError on both write routes and return the existing entry or a 409, not a 500.
recommended_actions.rationale: The replay check is device-scoped while the key is not, and the routes only flush and commit with no duplicate handling.

recommended_actions.action: Add a test with one user on two devices sending the same client_seq, and an alert on UniqueViolation counts on uq_transactions_idempotency_key.
recommended_actions.rationale: This would have caught the regression before or right after deploy; the first collision logged was 08:22.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm the cause after rollback by checking that the UniqueViolation count drops to zero.
recommended_actions.rationale: This closes the one inferred link, since no failing key has been paired with an existing row.

missing_evidence: No failing request's key was paired with an existing row from a different device_id; the last data step (S12) was skipped because the investigation was accepted. Logs carry neither client_seq nor the key, and rejected inserts are not stored.
The exception type of about 12 error lines outside the classified 08:20-09:00 window was not checked.
No metrics were queried for neon-postgres, upstash-redis or the external APIs, and no deploys were checked for them.
App version is not in the logs (user_agent is empty).
Several samples were partial or capped: device_id counts are lower bounds, transaction rows were capped at 50, and error line samples were limited.

what_changed.what_changed: The idempotency key construction dropped device_id, so keys are now unique per user and seq instead of per user, device and seq.

before.statement: Rows saved before 08:20 carry three-part keys such as 113:and-4cf0:351 and 132:ios-7ed8:254. The baseline hour had 1 500 on /transactions and none on quick-add.

after.statement: All 111 rows saved from 08:20:20 to 09:01:52 use the short user:seq key, and none use the old format. The first sampled UniqueViolation is at 08:22:31. There are 79 500s on /transactions and 9 on quick-add, which was 0 in the baseline.

changes_considered.change: deploy on fivo-api: commit ef5484e "idempotency: shorter keys, client_seq already identifies the entry" by github-actions
changes_considered.reason: Deploy dep-0414 (ef5484e) went live at 08:20:00Z, the same time as error onset. Its one-line diff drops device_id from the key. All post-deploy rows use the new key. The UniqueViolations on uq_transactions_idempotency_key began at 08:22 and there were none before. No other deploy or config change is recorded.
